questions.q: According to this lesson, can a deployment with zero technical defects still cause real business disruption?
options: No — if there are no technical defects, the deployment is by definition successful
Yes — deployment planning also involves sequencing, timing, and communication, and skipping any one can cause disruption even with flawless code
No — disruption only ever comes from a coding mistake
Yes, but only if the Change Advisory Board was never involved
questions.explain: A technically perfect deployment can still land in the wrong order, at the wrong time, or without warning the people affected — all non-technical failures.

questions.q: Why does deploying a scoped application before a dependency it relies on is active cause a problem, per this lesson?
options: It fails loudly and immediately, which is easy to catch
It can activate 'successfully' and only fail later, when a user triggers the feature that needed the missing piece
ServiceNow blocks any deployment with an unresolved dependency automatically
Dependencies never actually matter for scoped applications
questions.explain: The activation itself can succeed even though the dependency isn't there yet, so the failure surfaces later and is harder to trace back to the real cause.

questions.q: What does Conflict Detection add to deployment timing that simply checking a maintenance window on a calendar by eye does not guarantee?
options: It automatically flags when your planned change overlaps in time with another change touching the same Configuration Item
It automatically reschedules every change to the earliest open slot
It replaces the need for a maintenance window entirely
It only checks for conflicts between Update Sets, never between full application deployments
questions.explain: Conflict Detection specifically flags scheduling overlap on the same CI, catching a risk a human visually scanning a calendar could miss.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat notifying affected users as part of deployment planning rather than an optional courtesy?
options: Because users always prefer surprises over advance notice
Because a user who hits an unexpected change mid-task with no warning will treat it as an outage, regardless of how clean the deployment was underneath
Because notification is legally required for every ServiceNow deployment
Because it has no effect on how the deployment is perceived
questions.explain: From the business's point of view, an unannounced change that disrupts someone's workflow reads the same as a failure, even when nothing technical actually broke.

questions.q: What distinguishes a real deployment plan from a technical checklist, per this lesson's closing section?
options: A real plan only needs to confirm the code passed ATF tests
A real plan answers sequencing, timing, AND communication questions before the deployment runs — not just what order dependencies go in
A real plan is one that skips the Change Calendar to save time
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: A plan that only maps dependency order is still just the technical half of the job; timing and communication complete it.
